representation of audio, images, and text. The full dataset and
preprocessing code are available for reproduction of results and further
analysis at https://github.com/ku248/musictm.

One major obstacle when utilizing Linked Data lies in developing intuitive and user-friendly interfaces accessible to individuals who aren't technologically inclined. To address this, Ontodia enables diagrammatic data visualization, illustrated in this study with the Wikidata dataset. We've introduced enhancements to a natural language interface that facilitates the exploration and selection of entities within Ontodia, utilizing distributed representations of concepts. The integration proved challenging due to the sequential nature of word embeddings, which typically represent spatial relationships. To mitigate this, we've implemented a grid system, dividing the visual area into cells where each can contain one entity. This allows us to map word embeddings to grid cells, demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach, and suggest future improvements.

We've discovered a type of stable solitary wave in the nonlinear Schr\"{o}dinger equation, including cases with external influences such as defocusing transport and varying dispersion levels based on intensity. The proof of its longevity relies on a method of separating the equation into individual equations for phases and amplitudes, as well as a specific inequality derived from Hardy and Littlewood from 1940.

This collaborative approach in visual analytics aims to facilitate seamless interaction between humans and machines, according to various established frameworks. To bridge the gap between theoretical models and practical implementation, we have created Lotse, a system designed to simplify the incorporation of guidance methods into software and easily facilitate experiments. Using Lotse, researchers can quickly evaluate and compare different guidance methods without extensive development time, thus allowing for more efficient and widespread testing. Furthermore, Lotse's modular structure and broad support for various guidance methods enable in-depth analyses of the underlying concepts, while also promoting the development of more sophisticated guidance methods.

We've developed an innovative approach to coil design that accommodates a range of magnetic configurations, including three-dimensional stellarators. Our method utilizes several magnetic reconstruction frameworks to identify the most versatile coil sets. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this strategy by optimizing coil designs for both general efficiency and efficient use of material. This collaborative work between NCSU and Max-Planck/IPP integrates the REPRO coil placement tool and our novel optimization framework to reveal promising results.

Achieving uniform temperature distribution within catalytic fixed bed reactors is crucial for both efficient production and reaction stability. However, thermal instabilities often develop, particularly in beds packed with large particles, due to the occurrence of hot spots. To better understand these thermal instabilities, researchers used rapid magnetic resonance imaging to visualize the temperature distribution within a vertical gas-solid fixed bed. The imaging technique allowed for the determination of axial and radial temperature gradients, revealing temperature differences of up to 20 K in both large and small pores. The results showed that hot spots developed primarily in the upper sections of the bed, particularly near obstacles. Furthermore, the technique enabled the correlation of temperature fluctuations with flow turbulence and pressure drops. The authors note that while the temperature fluctuations were substantial, with averages around 5 K, they were not sufficiently large to significantly affect chemical reaction rates.

Within a cellular environment, proteins and nucleic acids autonomously separate, resulting in the spontaneous formation of membraneless droplets. This process underlies the development of numerous sub-cellular compartments. Droplets composed of the same materials but in different quantities behave uniquely, exhibiting varying droplet sizes or formation rates. A new theoretical framework has been introduced that explains these distinct behaviors, describing droplet formation through a competition between two opposing forces: an entropic drive to increase droplet size and a thermodynamic drive to minimize droplet size. This framework predicts that the equilibrium size of a droplet is determined by a balance between these forces, while dissipation plays a crucial role near droplet formation thresholds. Furthermore, the framework enables the calculation of droplet formation rates and demonstrates that droplets composed of shared components can exhibit a wide range of behaviors, even within a single cellular condition.

Using the Helioseismic and Magnetic Imager on the Solar Dynamics Observatory, we studied how a major leading sunspot rotated in NOAA AR 11429 during two powerful solar flares. A notable sunspot rotated in an unconventional direction, influenced significantly by two major solar eruptions. In the first flare, the sunspot rotated in an unconventional (reverse) direction, accompanied by the sunspot's magnetic polarization reversing, and a notable increase in the sunspot's area. However, the sunspot's rotation behavior in the second flare was more complex, with parts rotating conventionally and others in an unconventional manner. The conventional rotation areas experienced a notable decrease in the sunspot's area during this flare.

This note presents a new category of map functions known as oriented colored broken submersions, which forms the most basic type of map functions that adhere to the b-principle, and is nearly equivalent to the set of oriented submersions in 2 dimensions. It demonstrates that the Madsen-Weiss theorem, which is essentially a refined version of the Mumford Conjecture, can be proven solely through the application of a specific type of oriented colored broken submersion, known as oriented colored broken immersion, that satisfies a particular transversality condition, and depends on the outcome of two other key results: the Gromov-Mather theory and the Viterbo conjecture, whose proofs are already available.

This research involves comparing the efficiency of Balancing Domain Decomposition by Constraints (BDDC) and Algebraic Multigrid (AMG) methods for solving complex cardiac mechanics problems on various types of finite element grids. By modeling the mechanical properties of heart tissue using a non-linear elastic material, researchers can determine the tissue's mechanical properties through minimization of the energy function, using an iterative solver accelerated by a preconditioning technique. Although finite element methods are versatile, they are limited by large systems of equations resulting from the discretization of the problem. To overcome this obstacle, BDDC and AMG methods can significantly improve the solver's convergence, albeit with performance dependent on various factors such as grid structure, scheduling, and implementation. To ensure realistic simulations scale efficiently on large computers, this study uses small, medium, and large-scale finite element models with varying numbers of degrees of freedom. By optimizing the BDDC and AMG solvers on these models and performing computations on the Mont Blanc cluster, researchers were able to observe the methods' performance under realistic conditions, with the 3D models on two levels exhibiting better performance than those on six levels. Furthermore, due to the subdomain and interface scheduling complexity, the results were difficult to predict, but showed significant potential for improvement. Based on these findings, it appears that BDDC and AMG methods are viable options for solving large cardiac mechanics problems, with potential for substantial speed-ups in realistic simulations.

The ever-growing influence of user-generated content is significantly altering the digital landscape, while the increasing concern for intellectual property rights necessitates an in-depth examination of content creation and reuse patterns to devise effective, fair compensation systems for content creators. To address this challenge, we propose a comprehensive framework that aims to (1) identify and quantify content creation and reuse patterns, (2) uncover the evolution of these patterns over time, (3) reveal shared interests among groups within a system, and (4) develop collaborative strategies to achieve optimal results. By applying this framework to various social media platforms, such as Del.icio.us and Flickr, we provide detailed analyses and empirical findings that substantiate our approach.

Recently, proposed bianisotropic acoustic metagratings offer promising possibilities for passive acoustic wave manipulation, notably in flat acoustic lenses and ultra-high frequency ultrasound imaging. This concept, however, has not yet been implemented at ultrasound frequencies due to a lack of suitable materials. This study successfully demonstrates a functional acoustic microgating at a very high frequency of 100 MHz, an unprecedented achievement in this field. We achieve this by utilizing a two-photon lithography technique to manufacture advanced microstructures, integrating both water and air, within a polyurethane matrix. Through numerical simulations and practical experiments, we investigate the effectiveness of acoustic wave reflection and direction changes utilizing these microgating structures.

This paper primarily focuses on the long-term behavior of strong solutions to the two-dimensional compressible FENE dumbbell model. Utilizing the Fourier splitting technique, we demonstrate that the $L^2$ decay rate is given by $\ln^{-l}(e+t)$ and the fastest $L^2$ decay rate is $\ln^{-1}(e+t)$. Furthermore, we have established that $H^1$ and $L^3$ norms decay at a rate of $\ln^{-1/2}(e+t)$ as $t$ approaches infinity.

Implementing integrated access and backhaul (IAB) through wireless technology offers a promising way to build a mobile and indoor network. Although some IAB systems are still in the experimental phase, they show potential in supporting mobile services. To accelerate the adoption of IAB, we need to understand its limitations and how to overcome them in real-world scenarios. This work focuses on the issues surrounding IAB's practical application, specifically those related to installing IAB equipment outdoors and providing indoor services to mobile users. We examine two key problems: identifying the locations of users and providing services to them, and assigning frequencies to avoid interference. We propose algorithms and analytical models to tackle these issues, using frequency-hopping spread spectrum, which is a feature of many wireless technologies. Our analysis covers both centralized and distributed approaches to system management. By solving these problems, we can pave the way for using IAB in mobile IAB networks.

In this study, we conduct an extensive examination of five leading global optimization algorithms as a hyperparameter configuration problem to understand the overall impact of each variable on their performance. By utilizing three methods of sensitivity analysis, we analyze the behavior of 29 key parameters, evaluating their significance in interacting with problem characteristics, such as function complexity and dimensionality. The analysis reveals that the interplay between these parameters varies greatly depending on the specific characteristics of the optimization problems they are applied to, which has implications for their usage. The study provides quantitative data to guide the selection of relevant parameters for further investigation, potentially leading to more efficient tuning and evaluation processes.

The paper addresses misconceptions surrounding Jefimenko's equations, which are derived from Maxwell's equations, for a specific charge and current configuration obeying the continuity equation. It subsequently derives a non-radiative condition across inertial frames, consistent with the stability requirements of an atom, and establishes that this condition is analogous to certain relationships between charge, current, and the wave equations. The paper then demonstrates that these relationships lead to quantised electromagnetic field energy displaying the characteristics of the Balmer series.

Despite notable breakthroughs in reinforcement learning, its widespread use in
real-world settings remains limited due to several constraints. In order to overcome
these limitations and prepare future AI systems for continuous learning, a new
approach is needed. This approach requires a controlled environment for studying
longitudinal reinforcement learning scenarios. To this end, a novel simulation
platform called L2Explorer has been developed, which models a dynamic educational
setting where agents navigate through various tasks to accumulate rewards.
Throughout multiple learning sessions, the agent encounters altered task distributions
and must adapt to new situations seamlessly. This educational framework
accommodates multiple control strategies, offering valuable insights into the
effectiveness of different lifelong learning methods.

Liger, a next-generation infrared device at the W. M. Keck Observatory, will be one of the most sensitive optical-infrared observing facilities in the world when it launches in 2025. Liger will have a vast field of view of approximately 6.8 x 60 inches, enabling it to conduct numerous scientific studies simultaneously. Given the vast amount of data it will collect, processing this data at the telescope is crucial to enable real-time data analysis and publication of findings. Our team has developed a data processing system that runs on the Keck Interferometer Control system (KICS) and is in charge of data processing at the telescope. This paper outlines the design of Liger's data processing system, the algorithms used, and the software interfaces through which scientists can access their processed data while the telescope is in operation.

This study uncovers a broad class of non-trivial and smooth travelling waves that arise in the vicinity of the Couette flow in 2D Euler equation, at low regularity in vorticity $H^s$ for $s<3/2$. The velocity of these waves is directly proportional to their distance from the Couette flow. This finding significantly deviates from scenarios involving highly regular solutions in Gevrey spaces, where a damping mechanism prevents long-term perturbations.

We experimentally control the linear polarization of exciton-polariton condensates using optical traps with elliptical geometries that favor specific polarization modes. Due to anisotropic splitting in the cavity, ground state degeneracy is lifted, yielding fine structure modes along the trap's axis and orthogonal to it. These modes are selectively occupied by the condensate. Our results reveal a unique method for polarization control with potential applications in spin-based photonics and research on complex optical systems with adjustable coupling properties.

This study's primary objective is to provide evidence and disproofs for the deterministic Kardar-Parisi-Zhang type equations including non-local gradient elements. The specific focus lies within a particular class of nonlocal equation subclass that incorporates a unique fractional Laplace divergence. The key to this nonlocal framework is the understanding and representation of the fractional Laplacian through its corresponding stochastic driver, thereby allowing the application of established stochastic analysis tools. The paper concludes by identifying a critical condition required for the existence and uniqueness of solutions to these deterministic Kardar-Parisi-Zhang type equations.

The COVID-19 pandemic in South Africa exemplifies a severe infection surge beneath a lockdown environment. With a population of over 50 million people, the country's outbreak trajectory contrasts strikingly from other developed nations, primarily tracked through the Superscripted SARS-CoV-2 genome. In this study, we employ a data-driven approach to analyze available epidemiological data to derive a basic mathematical model for understanding the pandemic progression. We combine two distinct methods: (a) an ordinary differential equation-based SEIR model and (b) a Bayesian estimation procedure of the basic reproduction number (R0). We use these methods to develop a hybrid framework that allows us to understand the pandemic timeline, predict cases and deaths, assess the effectiveness of non-pharmaceutical interventions, and estimate R0 in the midst of a lockdown environment.

Freiman's 3k-4 theorem generally posits that if subsets A and B, of size k and comprised of integers, exhibit a sumset narrowness of at most r, then they inherently embody an affine slice of size 3k-4, defined by a linear transformation. In the specific instance where r equals one, it essentially asserts the existence of an affine line with at least k-4 elements, whose sumset equals A+b for some element b in B. We aim to demonstrate a verifying extension of this theorem for particular cases, particularly when both A and B contain exactly three elements, thereby invalidating a prior counterexample proposed by Tom Sanders.

In medical contexts, diverse information often arises from various sources, which when combined enables healthcare professionals to form more precise opinions. For retinal analysis, recent advancements have led to the integration of multiple imaging techniques such as color, infrared, and OCT. This research introduces a novel approach to fusing information from multiple modalities for the purposes of identifying glaucoma and diagnosing diabetic retinopathy. Unlike existing methods, our solution does not necessitate explicit feature extraction and can instead directly utilize raw modalities, which it then combines through a simple, efficient process. We test our approach using two datasets, and intriguingly, despite only being provided two modalities, it still achieves classification results comparable to those methods that utilize three modalities.

This research focuses on using computerized methods to identify the severity of COVID-19 from chest X-ray images. The severity of COVID-19 is typically determined by a patient's lung condition, specifically the inflammation caused by the virus, which can be reflected in changes to the chest X-ray image. The objective of this study is to pinpoint the image characteristics that distinguish mild and severe cases of COVID-19 from chest X-rays. By comparing the performance of different models, we found that exogenous features, which describe specific patterns in the image, are more effective than inherent features, which are derived from images through complex analysis, in classifying COVID-19 severity.

We analyze the transmission eigenvalue problem involving $u$ and $v$ in the Sobolev space $H^1(\Omega)$ associated with $(\Omega, \sigma, \mathbf{n}^2)$. Considering the case where $\Omega$ is a 2 or 3-dimensional ball, and the functions $\sigma$ and $\mathbf{n}$ only depend on the radial distance $r$, we find that there is a sequence of transmission eigenvalues $(\sigma_j^2)$ and corresponding non-trivial functions $(u_j, v_j)$ that possess specific symmetries. It is proven that $u_j$ and $v_j$ are uniquely normalized and localized near the $\partial \Omega$ and it is shown that as $j$ approaches the limit, $(\sigma_j^2, u_j, v_j)$ converges to a solution of an exterior Dirichlet-Neumann problem. Additionally, it is shown that the sequence $(u_j)$ converges in $H^1(\Omega)$ to a function that satisfies an equation involving the radial part of the Laplacian, and that this function is the limit of an interior and exterior Dirichlet problem.

To expand a dialogue system's capabilities and handle unknown user inputs, new intent discovery is crucial, allowing a dialogue system to recognize intentions it wasn't previously designed for. We develop a new intent discovery approach incorporating pre-training and a novel contrastive loss function. The first stage of our method involves a broad self-collected dataset and a pre-trained transformer model, both obtained from an unsupervised source. The second stage utilizes a contrastive loss to identify intentions the dialogue system hasn't encountered before. Our proposed approach outperforms current methods on two benchmark datasets.

The classical universal bundle functor W mapping from the category of simplicial groups in C to the category of simplicial sets in C lifts to a monadic structure on the category of simplicial groups in C, and this extension holds for simplicial algebras defined by any Lawvere theory that includes group theory.
In our analysis, we demonstrate that a finite group of order $r$ possesses no more than $$7.3722\cdot r^{\frac{\log_2r}{4}+1.5315}$$ subgroups.

This study re-examines the Adler-Bobenko-Suris H2 equation. In the context of a 3D loop group action, we identify a key element, namely a 2-parameter loop group element. We then derive a subset of continuum Toda lattice equations, along with a related tri-linear form, all based on specific conditions applied to this loop group element. Furthermore, we explore the connection between these conditions and the general hierarchy of the Toda lattice, revealing a notable equivalence in the context of the 'direct' and 'inverse' limits.

This paper delves into the source of difficulty in Visual Relationship Detection (VRD) due to false positive restrictions. By classifying each proposal's relationship with an object as 'owning' or 'associated with', we relax the requirement that a proposal can only belong to one relationship. This simplification enables us to identify a proposal's relationships more accurately and overcome the issue of false positives in VRD. Our approach has been successfully applied to the SpCy family of algorithms, which are designed for accurate semantic analysis. As a result, our model has achieved superior performance on the Minipose and COCO datasets.

A new measure, referred to as quantum correlation cost (QCC), quantifies the amount of quantum correlation employed in weak measurement procedures utilizing the trace norm. It's demonstrated that the QCC is directly linked to the trace-norm-based quantum discord (TQD) by a factor dependent on weak measurement strength. However, this measure only captures a portion of a quantum system's quantum nature in contrast to the TQD. Furthermore, our results reveal that remaining quantum features can be extracted not only via further von Neumann measurements but also through a series of infinitesimal, weak measurements along a particular direction. Consequently, we propose using QCC as a useful tool for effectively leveraging quantum correlation in quantum information processing.

Understanding social relationships is a crucial aspect of human comprehension. A social relationship graph can be utilized in various applications such as predicting someone's interests and identifying close friends. Traditional approaches rely on existing graph structures, which are often static and fail to accommodate dynamic relationships and changing personal characteristics. In contrast, relationship graphs based on visual data may better capture personal relationships, as body language and proximity cues are significant in social settings. However, generating social relationship graphs from visual data requires nodes with associated features that can represent individuals accurately. Existing methods either disregard visual information or focus excessively on facial features, neglecting the context. Moreover, they typically employ fixed, predetermined feature extraction frameworks, making it difficult to incorporate context-specific visual information. To address these limitations, we introduce an end-to-end network that learns to extract both face and body features from input images, utilizing a context-aware framework to map these features to a social relationship graph. Our approach is specifically designed for social relationship graph generation and is tailored to prioritize node features and edge connections effectively. In our experiments, our customized model consistently outperformed existing state-of-the-art methods by a significant margin.

Capturing long-range relationships in scene understanding is vital for numerous vision tasks. Although some models utilize self-attention mechanisms to indirectly model these relationships, they have limitations. In contrast, graph neural networks, with their ability to directly address relationships between any two nodes, are better suited for the task. However, most existing graph models assume a predetermined fixed structure, which is unsuitable for image recognition applications. In response, this paper proposes a new graph message-passing framework that adapts to the task at hand. This approach leads to a dynamic graph message-passing network, which outperforms current methods by a significant margin and achieves state-of-the-art results on various vision benchmarks.

Optimized hardware is often required in embedded systems, leading to a common operation called Multiple Constant Multiplication (MCM). An efficient and commonly used method for MCM is the Circuit Sizing approach, which reconfigures an existing adder circuit to perform multiplications at a lower cost. However, this method overflows and loses precision when dealing with large multiplicands or constants. To address this issue, a new algorithm is proposed, which allows for a predefined number of bits to be allocated to the multiplier and constant inputs. As such, the Circuit Sizing method can be applied without the risk of precision loss, while also minimizing the hardware cost. The proposed algorithm's performance is compared to existing solutions through benchmark tests.

The intersection of quantum computing and deep neural networks has recently given rise to a growing research field, known as quantum deep learning. Despite previously being separate entities, advancements have revealed that quantum circuits share parallels with artificial neural networks, paving the way for widespread adoption. This paper delves into the foundational and functional aspects of quantum deep learning, highlighting key concepts and their real-world applications. These applications include using quantum circuits for pattern recognition, analyzing complex data, and optimizing challenging tasks. The paper also identifies prominent research frameworks and outlines promising future research directions, such as integrating quantum circuits with neural networks and testing their performance on quantum hardware.

The radio frequency (RF) accelerator technology continues to be fundamental in 
high-energy particle physics experiments. This summary outlines the progress 
made in the last few years and highlights key areas for further exploration, 
presenting recommendations for future investigation and development in the 
process.

In the near future, physicists anticipate that the Large Hadron Collider (LHC) will discover new physics. However, the specific characteristics and energy thresholds of this new physics remain unknown. It's probable that insights gleaned from LHC data will require supplementary information obtained from a muon collider to make substantial breakthroughs. This paper outlines the progress, advantages, and obstacles of developing a muon collider, particularly a compact design with a luminosity capacity of 10 abase^-1, which would be well-suited as a follow-up to the FCC-hh.

We have determined the dispersion relations for relativistic fluid modes in various configurations - scalar, vector, and tensor - and found the differences between their behavior in divergence-based and relaxation-time-approximation models. Our comparison also shows correspondence with first-order causal theories and highlights how a specific divergence-based model can predict damped tensor waves. This aligns with kinetic theory's results. It's interesting that both hydrodynamic and holographic fluids display similar properties. These findings might provide a way to test hydrodynamic theories using gravitational wave signals.

Our research assesses whether the cosmic background of radiation detected by Keck Array and BICEP2 could be the result of radiation emitted by primordial black holes. Previous estimates by Arza and Hooper revealed that such a scenario is feasible, and we aim to expand upon their findings. Initially, we will determine the rate at which PBHs collapse and then establish the spectrum of gamma-ray emission resulting from this collapse. Subsequently, we will calculate the intensity of diffuse background radiation and compare it with measurements from CMB and BLMR. This comparison will enable us, like Arza and Hooper, to evaluate PBH collapse against existing data but with heightened accuracy.

Introducing the Virtual Secure Platform (VSP), a pioneering solution that brings together multi-opcode instruction sets and arbitrary-precision arithmetic within a sequential processor architecture, further enhanced by a fully pipelined design for improved efficiency and speed. The VSP framework seamlessly executes Heath's FLDO library operations in a versatile, application-independent manner, allowing developers to execute FLDO-based programs on encrypted input values. Our implementation showcases a virtual processor with a five-stage pipelined design, complete with a decoders section that accommodates both FLDO and Generalized Flipping codes under the Tripolar Approximate Arithmetic (TAA) scheme, providing up to 2.5 times faster execution compared to comparable approaches without optimized decoders.

Researchers investigate polynomial-time approximation schemes (PTAS) for solving specific constraint satisfaction problems, such as Maximum Independent Set or Minimum Vertex Cover on graph classes that have limited connectivity. A previously known PTAS for CSPs with restricted constraints, defined by a local constraint function, broke down in cases with complex interdependencies between variables. To overcome this limitation, a new PTAS is proposed for general-valued CSPs with sparsity, involving integer variables and local functions, significantly extending previous PTAS findings for CSPs with structured constraints.

Pre-trained language models possess the ability to capture syntactic information, as established in previous studies [Tenney et al., 2019, Jawahar et al., 2019, Hewitt and Manning, 2019]. We build upon this research by leveraging pre-trained models for unsupervised and few-shot parsing, aiming to minimize the need for annotated constituency trees. Our approach employs self-attention mechanisms within sequential models to identify constituent structures, as demonstrated in unsupervised recursive neural networks [Gupta and McAllister, 2014]. Furthermore, we utilize masked language modeling and sentence permutation to enhance pre-trained models' syntactic awareness in an unsupervised manner. In few-shot parsing, we apply finetuning on a small, annotated parsing dataset after pre-training. Notably, our model achieves comparable results with state-of-the-art parsers on the WSJ and PTB datasets, and even outperforms other few-shot parsing models, as tested on datasets such as SQuAD and CoMerge.

High-definition hyperspectral images, which capture more detail in city scenes, can potentially be leveraged by object detection algorithms beyond standard RGB vision. However, current object detection models are primarily designed for use with RGB images and are not easily adaptable to hyperspectral data due to the added computational complexity. To overcome this limitation, we develop a two-stage object detection framework that first segments regions of interest from the image with minimal labeling requirements, and then uses these areas to guide a standard RGB object detection model to refine the segmentation. This approach enables more accurate semantic segmentation in a wide range of city settings with limited annotation, outperforming leading object detection models and weakly-supervised segmentation methods in the HSNet dataset benchmark.

Internal dynamics of stars can lead to unusual photospheric patterns and activity levels, similar to those observed on the sun. We investigate these phenomena in greater detail, specifically looking at a subgroup of rapidly rotating stars with unusual properties. These stars, all located on the main sequence, exhibit high levels of surface activity and complex spin patterns, as indicated by Gaia DR2 and TEPS study data. Further analysis of these stars, using Gaia EDR3 and TEPS data, reveals significant changes in rotation rate and/or eccentricity. This subgroup consists of 21 stars from the main sequence and 13 off-ecliptic stars, primarily consisting of Hyades and Praesepe members. We find that about half of these stars show increased eccentricity, which could be a result of tidal forces, but also find that many of these stars are rapidly rotating within a day, exceeding the Spotted Reference Model rotation rate, especially when considering their age. This is particularly true for 35% of main sequence and 46% of off-ecliptic stars, and could indicate an unknown angular momentum redistribution process or an internal structure where the core is smaller than expected. Additionally, some of these stars may be experiencing engulment by a Jovian planet, as indicated by their location near or inside the habitable zone, which could lead to increased eccentricity and tidal forces, and result in the observed spin down and photospheric changes.

In algorithmic literature, the underlying computation model is typically implicit and assumed to be based on the RAM model. Despite being widely adopted, the RAM model lacks a solid theoretical foundation, characterized by inconsistent time complexity definitions and unpredictable behavior. Notably, combining two integers of size $n$ can take $\Theta(n)$ time under one addition-based model and just one step under another. This study aims to establish a unified set of basic operations for the RAM model and provide a systematic approach to time complexity, with a focus on single-bit operations. By introducing key properties, we demonstrate that the RAM model can efficiently perform a range of basic operations, including bitwise operations, modulo operations, and power calculations, and prove that sequential composition and loop control (conditional statements and counter management) are computationally efficient on the RAM model.

To tackle the data sparsity problem affecting session-based recommendation models that predict the next item users will choose, we propose a novel approach that leverages both session data and graph embeddings. Our method involves two stages: first, we develop a self-supervised session embedding technique, and then we employ these embeddings in conjunction with graph embeddings derived from an auxiliary graph. This graph is optimized to aggregate similar session embeddings and thereby amplify their predictive value. Our approach, which relies on a unique graph scoring strategy, can be trained end-to-end without the need for labeled data. Consequently, we encounter a paradigm shift in session-based recommendation, where graph embeddings play a pivotal role. Extensive experiments on diverse datasets reveal that our proposed method surpasses several established benchmarks.

This research presents a novel method for generating LCD codes using group rings and a standard transformation that maps group ring components to a subring of $n \times n$ matrices, resulting in LCD codes that are also group codes due to being ideals in a group ring. Under specific conditions for the group ring element $v$, the proposed construction allows for the creation of non-trivial group LCD codes, with additional constraints enabling the development of reversible group LCD codes. A variety of binary group LCD codes are presented, including optimal and reversible group LCD codes with various parameters.

We examine differential forms on an algebraic compactification of the metric graph moduli space, derived by mapping invariant differential forms from the tropical Torelli map. Our investigation focuses particularly on a specific form, which when evaluated at the metric graph moduli space identifies the Feynman integrands of scalar field theories in flat spacetime.

In various object categorization tasks, particularly in visually complex conditions, it has been demonstrated that recurrent neural networks (RNNs) can outperform feedforward models.  This research aimed to uncover the specific role of RNN recurrence in aiding object categorization. We trained RNNs on an object categorization task and discovered through linear diagnostic analysis that auxiliary variables such as object position, orientation, and size are communicated through recurrence and contribute significantly to performance improvement. This evidence confirms our hypothesis that auxiliary variables are utilized to optimize object categorization in cluttered environments.

Despite numerous studies on non-Hermitian topology, the influence of correlations remains a significant unresolved issue. We have explored the correlations' effect on a one-dimensional non-Hermitian system with a notable point-gap topology. Our results reveal that local correlations enhance the point-gap topology. We have developed a simplified approach for managing the correlations' impact and applied it to various scenarios, including the presence of a correlated non-Hermitian Hamiltonian and correlated non-Hermitian spin- orbit coupling. Ultimately, we have demonstrated that correlations can be leveraged to reduce the dimensionality of a system displaying exceptional point gap topology.

Recently, Golay complementary matrices have gained popularity due to their utility in omnidirectional precoding techniques. This research extends Golay complementary matrices to higher-dimensional spaces known as multi-dimensional Golay complementary arrays and presents novel construction methods for pairs and quadruples of GCA. A set of ring identities is introduced to facilitate these constructions. Specifically, it is shown that GCA pairs are possible when the dimensions of the underlying lattices are of the form $4u$ and 2, or when they are all of the form $2u$. When the dimensions are at least 4, 2, or 1, GCA quadruples can be constructed. These findings also lead to new GCM constructions of various orders.

Research on Higgs boson production is conducted, combining data from 2011 and 2012 LHC runs at different center-of-mass energies. The analysis considers both on-shell and off-shell Higgs boson decay to a quartet of electrons, muons, and $b$-quarks, utilizing Boosted Technics and a 2D scan method to determine signal efficiency. The findings are compared with Standard Model predictions, resulting in constraints on hypothetical non-Standard Model couplings between the Higgs boson and W and Z particles. The constraints are expressed in terms of the ratio of coupling strength to that of the corresponding fundamental interactions, with their values ranging from -0.38 to 0.40, with errors, for the non-Standard Model couplings in the context of a fifth force between Higgs boson and W/Z particles. The study also provides a minimum upper limit on the Higgs boson width of 16 MeV, with its value ranging from 0 to 26 MeV, with errors, above the Standard Model Higgs boson width.

Incorporating dimensionality reduction techniques, researchers address the complexities of analyzing numerous spectral bands within bi-temporal hyperspectral images. This study proposes a cutting-edge approach using a novel deep convolutional autoencoder that fuses features across hierarchical levels and receptive fields. By utilizing an unsupervised change detection technique, it overcomes the limitations of other label-dependent methods. By integrating various techniques to extract changes from the images, it significantly outperformed current state-of-the-art methods in unsupervised change detection across diverse datasets.

Consider the set $\mathcal{S}$ of squares and let $\mathcal{W}$ be a subset of natural numbers such that when you combine these two sets with addition, the result encompasses all natural numbers. In other words, $\mathcal{S} \cup \mathcal{W}$ needs to have every natural number as an element. The size of $\mathcal{W}$ is minimal when compared to similar configurations in various number system structures, such as 1-to-1 and density-based systems, which has been proven by distinct researchers in the past. In this study, we establish that if $\mathcal{S} \cup \mathcal{W}$ covers all natural numbers with the least amount of elements in $\mathcal{W}$, then $\mathcal{W}$ contains consecutive natural numbers.

Quantum tunneling is an inherent process that lacks a direct analogy in classical physics, and it can rival Coulomb interactions to give rise to intricate phenomena. In silicon, silicon carbide, and carbon nanotubes, precise control over tunneling is facilitated through the manipulation of crystal valley degrees of freedom. Valley states, interconnected by tunneling, are the foundation of design concepts such as quantum interference and controllable spin exchange. We have developed a technique that enables the measurement of valley-tunneled particles and their interaction with a valley from the same family, resulting in a notable increase in the tunneling rate. The technique has been effectively used to study the valley-tunneled particle's valence band structure and spin exchange between two valley states associated with different atoms. The results from these experiments align with theoretical predictions, offering valuable insights that can contribute to the development of innovative valley-based technologies.

Many optimization problems with inherent constraints, especially those involving non-linear relationships, can be efficiently solved by incorporating novel technological advancements into the design. Several influential research approaches, including reinforcement learning and evolutionary algorithms, have converged for solving such complex optimization problems. The latter method, in particular, suffers from a lack of theoretical underpinnings despite its effectiveness and widespread use. We propose a new framework, LibOPT, for open-source software implementation of optimization techniques, with a focus on evolving algorithms. The framework is utilized to establish a fundamental relationship between reinforcement learning and evolutionary algorithms, demonstrating their equivalence in certain scenarios. The results of our experiments, conducted using LibOPT, confirm the connection between the two approaches.

Given an algebraic variety X that has a transitive action from the group Aut(X), the highest degree of transitivity of this action is called the transitivity degree. This degree is denoted by the maximum value of m for which Aut(X) acts transitively m times on X. In cases where Aut(X) is m-transitive for any positive value of m, we define the transitivity degree to be infinite. This study involves determining the transitivity degree for specific varieties, such as quasi-affine toric varieties, and homogeneous spaces, while exploring related open problems and conjectures.

This study investigates the behavior of a free particle in a two-dimensional space with an non-commutative geometry, where the coordinates satisfy a specific mathematical relationship. To resolve the identity crisis that arises in non-commutative geometry, particularly for particles with zero mass, we utilize the concept of non-commutative differential operators and the properties of commutator operators. We derive expressions for a particle's wave function, energy, and momentum, and examine the implications of space geometry on these quantities. Additionally, we discuss the consequences of our findings for particles with spin.

We apply the two-photon absorption transient current technique to study
properties of wide bandgap materials at the bulk doping level without the
need for optical excitation. Utilizing a 120 fs laser at 800 nm, we investigate
properties of type-I diamond and demonstrate that its thermal conductivity
is significantly enhanced when the laser is directed perpendicular to the diamond
crystal's axis, rather than parallel to it. We provide an analytical explanation
for the observed enhancement, which is consistent across different diamond samples.

Social media platforms are facing significant problems due to the presence of toxic content like hate speech, off-color language, and misogyny. These difficulties have caught the attention of Natural Language Processing (NLP) researchers, who are working to address them with more effectiveness. In this study, we introduce the first ever dataset specifically tailored for detecting misogynistic content within Arabic language posts on social media. We further develop and test a range of sophisticated NLP models that can not only spot this type of content but also categorize it as well. Our research findings reveal that our proposed models achieved impressive results, accurately identifying misogynistic content about women and trans individuals 90% of the time, while accuracy for misogynistic content about women alone reached 92%.

This study centres around the solvability of a distinct class of fractional backward stochastic differential equations that take into account past influences within their generators, under Lipschitz condition it's demonstrated that the existence and uniqueness of such equations are assured. Furthermore, a key comparison theorem has been formulated.

We examine if controllers obtained using model-based Reinforcement Learning, which employs an environment model to find the optimal policy, remain robust and adaptable when dealing with slight environmental variations. Building upon the concept from PILCO, a method for probabilistic policy search, our research demonstrates that constraining the uncertainty in the Gaussian Process model's dynamics has a beneficial effect on policy updates and results in more resilient controllers. In addition, our findings highlight the practical advantages of this approach in a simulated robotic application.

Several key network communication challenges such as caching and computation are interconnected. A centralized caching approach seeks to mitigate network strain during peak access times, whereas distributed computation explores the balance between computation and communication in a distributed system. This paper proposes a comprehensive framework for developing caching and computation schemes tailored to arbitrary graphs and file distributions. Leveraging this framework, existing schemes can be seamlessly reinterpreted, and new, improved architectures can be systematically designed.

We establish a formalization of the Scott model in univalent type theory, assuming a dependent type of universes and a primitive induction principle for coicative functions. To achieve this, we define a relation for strict equality between partial functions and show that this relation is compatible with the structure of partial functions. Next, we construct the Scott domain as a type of non-decreasing and bounded partial functions, and prove that it satisfies the necessary properties for a complete partial order (cpo). We then extend the type of elements in the Scott domain to include a constant representing infinity, and define a means-ends relation that mimics the usual order on the Scott domain. Finally, we show that the means-ends relation is compatible with the structure of the Scott domain, and that the type of elements in the Scott domain is a complete lattice.

Hanzer and Muić's work on degenerate Eisenstein series cancellations has been built upon, 
extending their method and outcome to a specific set of Eisenstein series, 
specifically those formed from the combinations of two Speh representations 
$\Delta(\tau,m)|\cdot|^{s_1}\otimes\Delta(\tau,n)|\cdot|^{s_2}$ in $GL(m+n,\mathbb{A}_\mathbb{Q})$ for self-dual cuspidal automorphic representation $\tau$.

This research introduces a novel control method that leverages Control Barrier Functions (CBFs) to create a practical and efficient safety control strategy for mobile robotic arms. Unlike traditional safe control approaches which focus exclusively on ensuring compliance with hard constraints, our approach incorporates both a CBF term and a penalization term in the cost function. The penalization term is derived from a configuration-dependent cost function and uses the robot's configuration to mitigate the complexity of handling time-varying safety constraints. By optimizing for the minimum cost, the robot's control trajectory is determined in a way that strikes a balance between meeting safety requirements and minimizing expense. The existence and uniqueness of the solution to this optimization problem are demonstrated, and the developed strategy is shown to provide a continuous and differentiable control trajectory. The effectiveness of this method is illustrated through mobile robotic arm simulation scenarios.

Natural language processing, a crucial field of study, strives to comprehend text via digital analysis, despite the inherent imperfections arising from diverse forms of written and spoken language. This work delves into employing various graph-based methodologies for resolving the challenge of text summarization via a selective extraction technique. Two key indicators – sentence overlap and edit distance – are employed for gauging sentence similarity.

Researchers have suggested the application of quantum interferometry and information processing in Bose-Einstein condensates. However, the current understanding of BECs relies on complex descriptions, often through quantum field theory or nonlinear differential equations. These descriptions sometimes conflict with key principles in interferometry and information processing. Despite the challenges, some initial studies have explored the possibility of implementing quantum gates in BECs. These studies have used a specific type of gate, specifically the Hadamard gate, and required a specific type of interaction between particles, either in momentum or energy space. Our study takes a different approach, exploring the implementation of nonlinear quantum gates using a specific type of interaction in both momentum and energy space. We found that certain types of interactions can efficiently block certain types of states, and that the phase of the gas's wavefunction plays a crucial role in the gate's operation. Additionally, the number of particles in the gate affects its behavior in an unexpected way.

This paper aims to accomplish two distinct objectives. Firstly, it seeks to establish a unicity theorem for meromorphic mappings from a complete Kähler manifold to a complex projective space, under the constraint of limited intersection with hypersurfaces. Secondly, the paper aims to prove a unicity theorem for the case of nondegenerate meromorphic mappings that share a specified number of hyperplanes in a particular geometric configuration.

In a recent study, the concept of nondegenerate algebraic sets for a given polynomial system was introduced, and it is deemed an essential area of study for multiple applications. We have developed a new algorithm that identifies nondegenerate solutions to a polynomial system through signature-based solutions obtained from a multi-variable polynomial division algorithm. This algorithm calculates the nondegenerate locus of a polynomial system by analyzing the signatures resulting from various division operations of the ideal generated by the polynomial system. It employs previously introduced methods, such as degree lexicographic multi-variable polynomial division with a specified signature, to achieve this. The algorithm provides a theoretical framework for determining nondegenerate solutions, and it is also accompanied by a demonstrated implementation in the Mathematica software.

Direct photons have been measured at $p_T<5$ GeV/$c$ for midrapidity and most central events of Cu$+$Cu collisions at $\sqrt{s_{_{NN}}}=200$ GeV. By calculating the $e^{+}e^{-}$ excess above the baseline across a wide range of $p_T$ and collision centrality, a picture of photon production emerges that aligns with calculations from early stages of the collision. Additionally, transverse production patterns of $e^{+}e^{-}$ pairs show an asymmetry that increases with $p_T$ and is consistent with aspects that have quasi-free characteristics.

Our note brings Turan's tetrahedron problem into the realm of $\ell_2$-norm, yielding improved results over prior work by Matulis, Raspaud, and Zarankiewicz. We demonstrate that any $\ell_2$-norm of at least $3\sqrt{3}$ on a 4-partite complete graph with vertices $x_1, x_2, x_3, x_4$ and weights $w_1, w_2, w_3, w_4$ that sum to 1 is both necessary and sufficient. We achieve this improvement over the existing record of $4\sqrt{3}$ by translating the problem into a constrained optimization issue, applying a technique known as Lagrange multipliers to simplify it, and obtaining an inradius for the resulting shape, dubbed Type 4 tetrahedron.

Achieving a seamless visual experience and optimal system performance when displaying line joins on vector maps requires an efficient anti-aliasing technique, particularly at high zoom levels where fine details prevail. However, the limitations of OpenGL API hinder optimal rendering when using conventional anti-aliasing methods, leading to noticeable artifacts and reduced system speed. In response, we developed a direct rendering technique utilizing CPU and GPU resources in conjunction, which results in a substantial enhancement of both visual quality and rendering efficiency.

The multivariate interpolation operator is traditionally constructed using piecewise linear functions to approximate absolute differences between values. In this study, we develop a novel, transcendental interpolation function derived from the hyperbolic tangent, providing more precise approximations of functions that increase linearly with the distance. Building on this, we establish a new, piecewise interpolation operator that maintains monotonicity and preserves the original function's characteristics, such as continuity and convexity. This new operator surpasses the classical linear interpolation operator in accuracy while ensuring the same level of smoothness.

Pulsar halos are large-scale, high-energy emission structures, formed by the relativistic electrons produced in the wind flows of pulsar wind nebulae (PWNe). These electrons, created in the turbulent magnetic fields of the wind, interact with interstellar radiation fields, leading to a significant energy exchange. As a result, the wind electrons lose energy and are absorbed at a rate proportional to their energy, resulting in a characteristic energy-dependent absorption in gamma-ray spectra observed from some PWNe. This process is a universal phenomenon in the evolution of all PWNe, but its manifestation is only observable in a few sources. In the study, a search was made for this absorption in all known gamma-ray PWNe in the Galaxy using data from the Fermi Large Area Telescope. By analyzing paired PWNe, it was found that some show clear signs of this absorption, while others do not. Based on the findings, it was estimated that approximately 1 in 5 PWNe exhibit this characteristic and 1 in 10 exhibit a different, more intense radiation, a phenomenon commonly observed in some PWNe.

Transportation systems are frequently hindered by unpredictable weather conditions.
Current methods of weather prediction, using either a network of weather stations or
satellite imagery, are often too costly or require significant infrastructure.
Visual weather forecasting offers a more cost-effective and practical solution.
Previous studies have shown that Convolutional Neural Networks can accurately identify
the weather from images, but such tasks remain underexplored in terms of a wide
dataset and comprehensive evaluations. Our work addresses this gap by introducing the
Weather4M dataset, which classifies six distinct weather types (clear, cloudy,
rain, snow, fog, and mist/haze), and implements a novel data augmentation technique
using filtering and image transformation. Our analysis encompasses various network
architectures and techniques, including the impact of pre-trained models and
regularization methods.

Our analysis examines how climate change interest shifts among diverse groups and how their individual interests interconnect. Initially, we track the individual trends, followed by developing a cross-influence model that we then validate using a VAR model. Our results indicate significant fluctuations in the general public's climate change interest, as evident from our creation of a Climate Change Index for Europe and the US based on media mentions, whereas economists show relatively little interest as measured by prominent journal publications. Furthermore, scientists' interest remains relatively steady, as observed in citations of leading climate scientists. Institutions, represented by international organizations, display consistent interest.

Soft grippers are increasingly popular across various applications due to their flexibility and ability to grasp delicate objects. However, controlling them proves to be challenging because the relationship between finger position and force is difficult to predict. To address this issue, this research presents a novel approach that uses the Koopman operator theory to create a predictive model of the gripper's behavior. To facilitate online model development, the research also introduces a control strategy that adapts to changing finger positions in real-time. Through experiments, the proposed method has been successfully tested on a flexible gripper and has shown significant performance improvements when compared to traditional model-based control approaches.

One of the fundamental problems in science and engineering involves finding the lowest cost value for a given function, known as an optimization problem. Various numerical methods have been proposed to solve this problem, but the Gradient Descent method remains the most popular due to its simplicity and effectiveness. However, this approach faces challenges with local minima and slow convergence, particularly when near the optimal point. In response, researchers developed the Natural Gradient Descent method to improve performance across multiple domains, but it comes with its own set of limitations. This study aims to overcome these limitations by introducing a new algorithm, the Hyperbolic Gradient Descent method, which boasts improved efficiency and scalability capabilities. A thorough mathematical analysis confirms that this algorithm surpasses the stability and convergence thresholds of previous models, including the Natural Gradient Descent method. Furthermore, our experimental findings validate the efficiency and scalability of the Hyperbolic Gradient Descent method in various practical applications.

High-energy sources, including those thought to be massive active galactic nuclei, are found at the center of a galaxy called J2102+6015, which is observed at a distance of approximately 6.8 billion light years from Earth due to the galaxy's movement. Researchers have discovered a strong radio signal originating from the center of the galaxy, which is only about 35 parsecs in diameter, indicating that the signal is less than 300,000 years old. This suggests that the radio signal is not yet obscured by intergalactic dust and allows for direct observation of the environment surrounding the source. High-resolution imaging of multiple frequency bands, combined with sophisticated data analysis, indicates a strong, compact signal in the center of the galaxy and several smaller signals at a significant distance from the center. This observation is consistent with a young and powerful energy source, which is likely to be an extremely bright and short-lived object in space, also known as an AGN. This is one of only a handful of such observations at such great distances, offering valuable insights into the early stages of galaxy development.

Non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) patients' five-year survival prospects significantly depend on the tumor's pathological stage. Accurately identifying and classifying NSCLC patients based on CT scans alone can be challenging, especially for early stage patients. To improve accuracy, our study integrated CT image features with patient demographics and clinical data, utilizing a multimodal framework that adapts to varying data availability. We demonstrated the effectiveness of our approach in achieving high cross-validation accuracy across different data completeness levels. Furthermore, our model's open-source code and clinical data can be easily replicated with publicly accessible resources.

A well-designed state representation is crucial in the learning process of Reinforcement Learning. Natural language can be utilized in numerous tasks to either represent the state or constitute it entirely. This overview focuses on the techniques employed by researchers to create natural language state representations, underscoring the need for more transparent and contextualized models, thorough justification of design choices and assessments of the relative effectiveness of varying methodologies.

A novel approach combining machine learning is introduced, enabling the accurate reconstruction of high-redshift cosmological density perturbations through observed quasar spectra analysis. By leveraging sophisticated simulations of cosmic structure formation, a substantial synthetic dataset is generated and fed into a machine learning algorithm. This algorithm, comprising multiple steps, distills the reconstructed density profiles into a predictable output from the quasar spectra. Assessment of the method's effectiveness involves comparing reconstructed and actual density profiles on multiple scales, while also considering potential network limitations and noisiness of the input data. Although initially derived from simplified cosmological simulations, our method can be readily adapted to address questions beyond those related to quasars and density reconstruction, including inferences about the circumgalactic medium and the distribution of heavy elements around high-redshift galaxies.

This paper examines certain types of non-weight modules connected to Lie algebras of the Weyl type. Firstly, we establish the characteristics of modules whose restrictions to $U(\frak h)$ are one-dimensional over Lie algebras representing differential operators on a circle. We then identify the requirements for the irreducibility of tensor products between certain types of modules, including modules representing differential operators and modules representing loop algebras.

Social media monitoring through sentiment analysis on platforms like Twitter enables
organizations and individuals to comprehend the overall public opinion on specific topics.
As a result, analyzing public sentiment has become increasingly vital for making informed
business and political decisions. With an abundance of data available on Twitter, a sentiment
analysis model can be developed to quickly and efficiently determine the prevailing mood
of the general public. In this study, we present a basic LSTM model for Twitter sentiment
analysis, comparing it to other established classification algorithms like Logistic Regression
and Random Forest. Our experiments showcase the effectiveness of the LSTM model,
which outperforms other models in achieving a high accuracy of 92% after data preprocessing.

Recent breakthroughs in open-dialogue models have made it possible to achieve human-like conversation performance with limited optimization, but their capabilities are still restricted to basic interactions. To expand these models and tailor them to specific requirements, our strategy involves defining a clear specification for desired conversational behaviors. Specifically, we outline the specifications for a role-based system that can understand and process user queries related to a particular topic, ensuring relevant and coherent responses are produced. To achieve this, we leverage large-scale language models, developing a set of specialized tools to enhance their performance in our targeted application. The effectiveness of our approach is demonstrated through comprehensive evaluation metrics focusing on the alignment between system responses and user queries, as well as their overall quality and coherence.

The binary black hole merger's aftermath leaves a lasting mark on space-time known as gravitational wave memory, and multiple events create a background of residual disturbance known as the stochastic gravitational wave memory background (SGWMB). Researchers have found that this phenomenon can be generated through the accumulation of gravitational wave memory from numerous events, and the amplitude of SGWMB is controlled by the square root of the number of occurrences, rather than the total count directly. The accumulation of SGWMB occurs more quickly than gravitational wave background (SGWB) caused by binary black hole mergers, and multiple observations could reveal SGWMB more easily.

A hypothetical supersymmetry framework offers a plausible explanation for why large particles weren't discovered by the Large Hadron Collider. If this framework is correct, a phase transition occurring during the cooling of the universe may break supersymmetry, which could also produce ripples at an observable intensity. Additionally, this transition may create dense objects called black holes with a mass similar to that of stars. In a theoretical scenario, these black holes could eventually emit energy at an extremely high rate, potentially detectable by radio telescopes. This theoretical scenario could also be consistent with another hypothesis stating that very heavy particles originally accounted for matter's asymmetry, a concept known as peer-scale leptogenesis.

A reliable and efficient communication system known as semantic communication strives to minimize data transfer and ensure that receiver and transmitter have a shared understanding of the message. As a new approach, this research combines an emergent language system based on a signaling game with a neuro-symbolic reasoning method to ensure that only relevant data are transmitted from the transmitter to the receiver. To achieve this, a common understanding of terms must be established through a language developed by both parties via a game involving signal transmission. Once agreed upon, the transmitter only sends the message essence, as the receiver can interpret the terms from the transmitted data. To model this process, a neural network and a set of rules are used to simulate the language development and transmission processes. Results show that only about 20% of the data need to be transmitted from the transmitter to the receiver, resulting in significantly reduced energy consumption and data transfer delays.

We present a new hybrid model for word prediction, combining the strengths of Naive Bayes and Latent Variable models. The approach leverages the local language context and part-of-speech tagging, exploiting unobserved bigram and trigram patterns to enhance the predictive power. A step-by-step analysis and mathematical justification underpins the model's development. Comparative evaluations on both synthetic and real-word datasets demonstrate the efficacy of this hybrid method.

Recent advancements in Session-based recommendation systems have gained popularity due to their ability to handle various session-based scenarios. These systems, being straightforward and efficient with high performance in online settings, have become preferred choices for real-time personalization tasks. This paper proposes a new approach, Two-stage Candidate Rank (TCR), an improved SBR framework that surpasses existing solutions. TCR enhances candidate selection and recommendation quality through two key steps: initially, filtering unwanted suggestions with Candidate Rank Embedding; secondly, re-ranking top choices based on a dynamic, context-aware score. Comprehensive experiments on three diverse datasets showcase TCR's superiority, highlighting its potential to be a reliable and reliable method for real-world SBR applications.

We examine a concentrated collection of active colloids that form various structures, including clusters of active colloidal molecules, which are formed when multiple colloids bond together. By using minimal models, we discover that active colloidal molecules tend to develop within activity gradients, with their shape largely influenced by the balance between their internal structure and the surrounding activity level. When these colloids interact through rejection forces, they prefer denser formations, whereas increased activity tends to break them apart, resulting in smaller clusters, as per Einstein's diffusion theory. Furthermore, we find that active colloidal molecules can assume various configurations, such as rod-like, triangular, tetrahedral, and diamond shapes, with their stability largely influenced by the activity level and their internal structure.

A thorough approach is outlined for simulating single-phase flow in fractured porous media. The proposed method consists of three core components: generating an accurate 3D mesh of a fracture network, solving governing equations, and validating the model's effectiveness. To create the mesh, a fracture surface is defined using a distance field method, which allows for smooth and continuous interpolation of fracture surfaces. The mesh generation process is fully automated and adaptable to any fracture configuration. The DDFD method is then employed to solve the governing equations, which involves converting the weak form of equations into a discrete algebraic system. The model's performance is then validated through several numerical experiments, which demonstrate good agreement with established laboratory and field data.

This research focuses on maintaining stability and collision avoidance for mobile robot clusters by employing a distributed, Centroid-Based Point Set Registration algorithm on each drone. When a drone detects an approaching entity, its vision is split into the formation and the incoming object, with their features compared using a registration metric to prevent collision. By adjusting its velocity, the drone modifies the formation's position while keeping its shape, achieving collision avoidance without disrupting the cluster. A study on the effectiveness and efficiency of this method has been conducted using simulation.

This research explores various spectral characteristics of the Seidel matrix associated with a connected chain graph, demonstrating that $-1$ is always an eigenvalue, while other eigenvalues may have a multiplicity of at most two. We also derive the characteristic polynomial of the Seidel matrix and present a limit theorem as the graph's diameter tends to infinity. Notably, we establish that the Seidel matrix's spectral radius is bounded by the square root of the graph's parameter $\omega$. Additionally, we examine the relationship between the matrix's eigenvalues and the parameter $\omega$, and compute the characteristic polynomial modulo 2.

In our investigation, we focus on a mean-field optimal control issue for stochastic differential equations featuring time-delay, which are influenced by fractional Brownian motion. To establish necessary and sufficient criteria for the existence of a unique optimal control, we draw upon the fractional Brownian motion's predictable representation property and characteristics of stochastic integrals. Additionally, our study demonstrates that when the memory parameter of the fractional Brownian motion is between 0.5 and 1, the resulting fractional Brownian motion can be replaced by an equivalent alpha-Brownian motion, thereby facilitating a deeper understanding of its properties.

We've developed a unique, detailed two-parameter set of finite-band Jacobi elliptic
potentials that correspond to the non-self-adjoint Dirac operator, seamlessly combining
the principles of unboundedness and positive deficiency index.

RSUs are a vital component in V2X communication, facilitating information exchange among road users through ROBs. Although vehicle relays can enhance network coverage and capacity, they are not considered in this discussion. We instead examine the performance of vehicular networks that include only RSUs and vehicles, acting as relays, to augment network capabilities. A two-dimensional analytical model is developed, accounting for vehicle speeds and lane changes, and expressed through the use of probability density functions. The analysis focuses on key metrics, including average user throughput, delay, and network fairness, with results indicating that these metrics are largely unaffected by RSU distance. Nevertheless, vehicle speed significantly impacts throughput and delay. Given these findings, network designers can optimize vehicle relays to maximize performance, by positioning them at distances that minimize the standard deviation of user delay.

Wikipedia's ultimate goal is to be an authoritative reference on various topics.  However, due to a limited number of editors and a vast amount of articles, only 0.6% of Wikipedia's content has been verified as reliable.  The rest is considered low quality, which readers may not be aware of.  Notably, there's a shortage of volunteers willing to contribute by labeling articles as high or low quality, which is crucial for informing readers.  Through close analysis of Wikipedia's editing process, we've developed an system that can automatically mark articles as high or low quality based on editing patterns, which in turn are linked to article content.  Our approach successfully identified the key factors influencing article quality with a high level of accuracy and consistency, even when applied to articles that have never been edited.  In experiments, our system outperformed other methods that rely solely on article content or reader feedback, and performed quality assessment with an accuracy of 55% when generalizing to all articles.

Knowledge distillation is a successful method for accelerating deep neural networks by training a compact model to mimic the behavior of a high-capacity network. Traditionally, this relies on having access to the original network's training data and parameters, which isn't always feasible due to storage or privacy constraints in real-world applications. This study introduces decision-based black-box knowledge distillation, allowing a model to be trained on the behavior of a network whose internal workings are inaccessible, as long as it produces classification outputs. When access to the original data is possible, a training sample's effectiveness is the amount of information its classification outputs reveal about the network's behavior. This study proposes several approaches to quantify this information and uses them to train a compact model to replicate the original network's behavior under these circumstances. The study demonstrates that decision-based black-box knowledge distillation is just as effective as traditional knowledge distillation and achieves comparable results to the original network itself. Additionally, the study highlights that decision-based black-box models can provide equivalent performance to network fine-tuning, but with the advantage of reduced computational requirements.

Researchers have observed the $B^0_s\to\bar{D}^0 K^0_S$ decay mode for the first time, and have also gathered evidence for the $B^0_s\to\bar{D}^{*0} K^0_S$ decay mode, by analyzing 37.2 $\text{fb}^{-1}$ of LHCb data collected during proton-proton collisions at 7 and 8 TeV. The branching fractions for these decays are calculated as follows: The $B^0_s\to\bar{D}^0 \bar{K}^0$ branching fraction is estimated at $1.10 \pm 0.11 \pm 0.03 \pm 0.14$%, and the $B^0_s\to\bar{D}^{*0} \bar{K}^0$ branching fraction is estimated at $0.99 \pm 0.24 \pm 0.11 \pm 0.12$%, with the given uncertainties stemming from LHCb, the PDG, and the $B^0_s$ decay mode itself respectively.

The $C^*$-algebra formalism of topological T-duality developed by Mathai and Wulkenhaar is used to give a unified treatment of classical T-duality on twisted tori, encompassing both integer and non-integer radius scenarios.

Reinforcement learning efficiency can be significantly enhanced through imitation learning by leveraging expert guidance. However, relying on expert demonstrations is often impractical or too costly due to the high expense of gathering them. In this research, we introduce a novel approach, called co-imitation learning, where multiple students collaboratively learn from a limited number of expert actions without requiring numerous demonstrations. By sharing knowledge, the expert uniquely corrects any discrepancies between the students' actions and the optimal policy, effectively utilizing the diverse experiences gained from interacting with each other. We provide a range of experiments supporting the efficacy of co-imitation learning, including environments like gridworld and the game of Tetris, where we observe that just a few expert inputs suffice for the students to converge towards the optimal behavior.

This paper proposes a metric function that yields an optimal performance on average, which significantly reduces decoding computation while maintaining superior error-correction performance for polarization-adjusted convolutional codes. When using our proposed metric, the PAC decoder's computational load is analogous to that of a sequential decoder. We also present an efficient method for calculating the proposed metric, which involves deriving upper and lower bounds on the PAC code's relative delay and sequential decoder's computation, respectively. These bounds can be recursively calculated to facilitate efficient PAC code design and optimization.

This project tackles the complex problem of simultaneously monitoring the positions and shapes of hands and objects in a sequence of depth point cloud data, starting from the known poses in the initial frame. To achieve this, we've developed a network that utilizes a simplified and efficient representation of hand and object shapes, allowing it to accurately track and reconstruct their configurations over time. Our approach is robustly trained on a vast synthetic dataset and is then evaluated on both a large dataset of realistic scenarios and an even larger collection of in-the-wild scenarios, outperforming existing methods and demonstrating the ability to provide precise joint location, shape, and pose reconstruction with minimal error.

This study employs the modular reduction technique to a Coxeter group of rank 4 featuring a spherical representation with a 2-interlacing property, utilizing the case of prime modulus 7. The resulting reduced system is then analyzed to derive an explicit matrix representation for a 7-modular group of order 336, which corresponds to a noncrystallographic tail-triangle group.
